newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian communist Duma head says Chubais must go.
newsitem.headline: Russian communist Duma head says Chubais must go.

text.p: The communist head of Russia's lower house of parliament on Wednesday called on President Boris Yeltsin to sack chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais, saying he would not work with him in a new consultative body, Interfax news agency said.

Gennady Seleznyov, chairman of the State Duma, issued the protest against Chubais because of the appointment on Tuesday of businessman Boris Berezovsky as deputy secretary of Yeltsin's policy-making Security Council.
The newly-formed consultative council -- aimed at smoothing over political differences between the executive and the legislature -- was due to hold its first meeting this Friday.
It consists of a "permanent four" -- Seleznyov, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, Chubais and Yegor Stroyev -- the speaker of the Federation Council upper chamber.
Seleznyov said Chubais, who has had a big influence over Kremlin affairs while Yeltsin prepares for heart surgery, must have been behind Berezovsky's appointment to the Security Council.

Berezovsky, 50, is a controversial figure with business interests ranging from car dealerships to television. Seleznyov said he had used his position on the board of the biggest state television channel to stage an "anti-Russian information coup".
